svg.title: Where configuration and secrets of a flow live
svg.desc: Four places from left to right. The solution in Git holds only definitions: the flow, connection references by logical name, and environment variable definitions with harmless defaults; no connection, no value of Test or Prod, no secret. The deployment settings file per environment holds connection IDs and environment variable values; for a secret variable the value is the path of a Key Vault secret, not the secret. The target environment holds the connections, created once per environment by an administrator, with the credential stored inside the connection. Azure Key Vault, one per environment, holds the secret itself; the Dataverse service principal and the people who create the variable have the role Key Vault Secrets User. At run time the flow calls the unbound action RetrieveEnvironmentVariableSecretValue with Secure outputs on; the next action that uses the value has Secure inputs on; the run history shows that content is not shown because of the security configuration. A bottom row lists five rules: nothing secret in the definition; values per environment in the settings file; secure inputs and outputs wherever a secret or personal data passes; whoever can edit a flow can use its connections; rotate credentials from the register before they expire.
svg.text: Definitions travel; values, connections and secrets stay where they belong

1 Nothing secret in a definition: no key in an expression, a header, a URL or a parameter default.
2 What differs per environment is an environment variable or a connection reference, with its value in the settings file.
3 Secure inputs and outputs wherever a secret or personal data passes. They hide; they do not encrypt or restrict use.
4 Whoever can edit a flow can use its connections for anything. Edit rights on flows are access to data.
5 Credentials have an owner and an expiry date in the register, and are rotated before, not after.
